semantic_adjudication.reason: NL2 ('If the signal transmission fails, it proceeds to the operational state.') is bound by the transition-group NL-GROUP-NL2-BRAKING-ALTS to a BrakingState->OperationalState edge. The complete exact source inventory (exact_source_inventory.transitions rows tr_0002-tr_0007) and closed FCSTM inventory (inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions lines 13-18) show no such edge exists: BrakingState's only outgoing edges go to ClampingState (Entering_Clamping_State) and InitialState (Signal_Feedback_Sent). The S2 backend receipt confirms verdict=false for source=BrakingState, target=OperationalState with an explicit counterexample record. This is a definitive negative inventory fact, not a predicate-availability gap, so grounding is established. However, the same NL2 text is plausibly read as scoped to the Initial State's own branching (since transition:line:14 realizes exactly the Signal_Transmission_Fails-triggered edge but from InitialState, not BrakingState), which is a second competent semantic reading of the sentence's source anchor that the supplied dossier itself raises as a strongest_rebuttal; this alternative is compatible with the same underlying facts (the edge exists, just from a different source), so it is undercutting rather than rebutting, and it survives as a genuine competing reading rather than being excluded by an explicit contract term.
semantic_adjudication.strongest_defeater: A competent alternative reading treats NL2's three sentences as all scoped to the Initial State's branching rather than a Braking State branch, since the closed model instead wires the Signal_Transmission_Fails-triggered edge (transition:line:14) from InitialState to OperationalState. Under that alternative scope binding, tr_0003/transition:line:14 would satisfy an Initial-State-scoped version of this guard/endpoint obligation instead of a Braking-State-scoped one, leaving a second competent semantic reading of which source state NL2 actually binds to, even though the contract as extracted binds the alternative to a Braking State source, under which no such edge exists.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: NL2 requires an exact BrakingState -> OperationalState transition guarded/triggered by signal-transmission failure so that while braking, a transmission failure routes the machine to the Operational State.

response.reason:
NL1 is descriptive context establishing the model's purpose (final execution unit for train braking), with no independently violable obligation. NL2 establishes an initial-entry to the braking state (from an implied root/initial pseudostate), a conditional endpoint to operational state on signal-transmission failure, and a return endpoint to the initial state upon signal feedback; the shared source for these branches is the braking state itself (entered via signal). NL3 establishes a sequential endpoint from braking state to brake caliper clamping state, continuing the discourse after entering braking state. Distinct transitions are represented as separate transition_endpoints contracts plus a transition_groups row capturing the shared-source alternatives from BrakingState (to OperationalState and back to InitialState is actually a different source - see below). I treat: (a) initial_entry contract for root/system -> initial state -> braking state pathway: actually the model's initial pseudostate enters the Initial State (explicit state), then upon receiving brake signal transitions to Braking State. NL2's "transitions from the initial state to the braking state" is an explicit transition endpoint (source=Initial State, target=Braking State), triggered by "receives a brake signal" (event). The "if signal transmission fails, proceeds to operational state" branches from Braking State (a different source, since it says "it" continuing from braking state context) -- but grammatically "it" refers to the basic braking device, and the alternative is presented right after the primary transition, suggesting it's an alternative outcome of the same signal-transmission attempt occurring while in Braking state. I model this as a separate endpoint contract source=Braking State, target=Operational State, guarded/triggered by signal transmission failure. The "once signal feedback is sent, it returns to initial state" is another endpoint from Braking State (or Operational State?) back to Initial State; given sequence, feedback happens after braking, so source=Braking State, target=Initial State. NL3 explicitly states after entering braking state, transitions to brake caliper clamping state, giving a further endpoint source=Braking State, target=Brake Caliper Clamping State. All these transitions share source Braking State except the very first (Initial State -> Braking State), so I form a transition_groups row for source=Braking State with alternatives: Operational State (on failure), Initial State (on feedback), Brake Caliper Clamping State (on entering, i.e. immediately). This preserves ordering and coreference without inventing evaluation content.</reason>

arguments.reason:
NL1 is descriptive context establishing the model's purpose (final execution unit for train braking), with no independently violable obligation. NL2 establishes an initial-entry to the braking state (from an implied root/initial pseudostate), a conditional endpoint to operational state on signal-transmission failure, and a return endpoint to the initial state upon signal feedback; the shared source for these branches is the braking state itself (entered via signal). NL3 establishes a sequential endpoint from braking state to brake caliper clamping state, continuing the discourse after entering braking state. Distinct transitions are represented as separate transition_endpoints contracts plus a transition_groups row capturing the shared-source alternatives from BrakingState (to OperationalState and back to InitialState is actually a different source - see below). I treat: (a) initial_entry contract for root/system -> initial state -> braking state pathway: actually the model's initial pseudostate enters the Initial State (explicit state), then upon receiving brake signal transitions to Braking State. NL2's "transitions from the initial state to the braking state" is an explicit transition endpoint (source=Initial State, target=Braking State), triggered by "receives a brake signal" (event). The "if signal transmission fails, proceeds to operational state" branches from Braking State (a different source, since it says "it" continuing from braking state context) -- but grammatically "it" refers to the basic braking device, and the alternative is presented right after the primary transition, suggesting it's an alternative outcome of the same signal-transmission attempt occurring while in Braking state. I model this as a separate endpoint contract source=Braking State, target=Operational State, guarded/triggered by signal transmission failure. The "once signal feedback is sent, it returns to initial state" is another endpoint from Braking State (or Operational State?) back to Initial State; given sequence, feedback happens after braking, so source=Braking State, target=Initial State. NL3 explicitly states after entering braking state, transitions to brake caliper clamping state, giving a further endpoint source=Braking State, target=Brake Caliper Clamping State. All these transitions share source Braking State except the very first (Initial State -> Braking State), so I form a transition_groups row for source=Braking State with alternatives: Operational State (on failure), Initial State (on feedback), Brake Caliper Clamping State (on entering, i.e. immediately). This preserves ordering and coreference without inventing evaluation content.</reason>

candidates.observed: Deterministic facts show ClampingState (line 10) and ClampingLoseState (line 11) are both reachable from the initial state but have zero outgoing FCSTM transitions (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING diagnostics; verify_facts deadlock checks refuted with outgoing_count=0). Neither is declared a final/terminal state in the canonical source (final_states=[]), so both function as unmodeled permanent halts in an otherwise continuously operating control loop.
candidates.reason: NL1 frames the whole model as a live, ongoing train braking control device, and NL3 requires the machine to progress into the Clamping state as part of that operating loop; the deterministic frontier facts show this reachable target (and the parallel ClampingLoseState leaf) has no way to continue or return to normal operation, which is a distinct behavioral-consequence defect from the already-satisfied endpoint-existence obligation.
candidates.requirement_quote: After entering the braking state, the system transitions to the brake caliper clamping state.
candidates.strongest_rebuttal: The NL text never explicitly states that the Brake Caliper Clamping State must resume behavior after clamping; the sentence 'After entering the braking state, the system transitions to the brake caliper clamping state' only describes reaching the state, so a competent reading treats ClampingState as an intentional narrative endpoint of this segment, and the underlying frozen predicate registry has no dedicated deadlock predicate for arbitrary leaf states absent an explicit progress/response clause, which is why this remains a predicate-null W1 candidate rather than a V1-backed claim.
candidates.title: Reachable Brake Caliper Clamping State and Clamping Lose State are permanent dead ends with no outgoing continuation

result.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequence: root reachability, event-consumer coverage, dead-end/frontier facts, cross-wrapper reachability, and stable termination. All five FCSTM states (InitialState, BrakingState, OperationalState, ClampingState, ClampingLoseState) are reachable_from_initial=true per inspection_equivalent_facts.reachability, and all five declared events have a reachable consumer transition, so root reachability and event-consumer coverage contracts (NL-CONTRACT-REF-001..004, REF-006/007/008) are satisfied at the reachable-consumer level and produce no candidate from this lens beyond termination analysis. The only behavioral-consequence issue is that ClampingState (the NL3 endpoint target, an operating/intermediate state entered from BrakingState) is a reachable leaf with zero outgoing transitions (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING, deadlock check refuted with outgoing_count=0), and ClampingState is not declared as a terminal/final state in the source or FCSTM (final_states=[] in canonical IR). Since NL3's transition_endpoints contract requires reaching Brake Caliper Clamping State as an operating continuation within the braking behavior (not an explicit NL termination role), I do not force a termination candidate on NL-CONTRACT-NL3-ENDPOINT-1 itself. Instead I derive one additional deadlock_freedom contract for the machine's overall operating continuation scope, covering both ClampingState and the similarly dead-end ClampingLoseState leaf, using predicate_id=null W1 since no explicit NL progress/response clause exists to anchor V1 with full confidence, though the deterministic LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING/deadlock-refuted facts are the closest available V1-style evidence and are cited as such. No forbidden-scope entry, cross-wrapper reachability defect, or bounded-response trace obligation is established by the supplied NL; the machine is flat (hierarchy_level=flat, one composite root, no concurrent regions), so no wrapper/region reachability issue applies. The NL3 target binding to ClampingState is exact via the FCSTM body annotation and source trace, recorded in semantic_bindings with its model_element_ref.

issues.basis: exact_source_inventory.transitions rows tr_0002-tr_0007; inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions lines 13-18; NL2 quote and transition group NL-GROUP-NL2-BRAKING-ALTS alternative ALT-NL2-OPERATIONAL.
issues.expected: An exact transition BrakingState -> OperationalState guarded by 'signal transmission fails' must exist so that while braking, signal-transmission failure routes the machine to the Operational State.
issues.observed: The complete exact source inventory and closed FCSTM inventory contain no BrakingState->OperationalState transition. The only Signal_Transmission_Fails-triggered transition (tr_0003 / transition:line:14) originates from InitialState, not BrakingState. From BrakingState the only outgoing edges are to ClampingState (Entering_Clamping_State) and to InitialState (Signal_Feedback_Sent).
issues.reason: The transition-group NL-GROUP-NL2-BRAKING-ALTS establishes Braking State as the shared source of the signal-transmission-fail alternative; the complete exact source and closed inventories show this exact edge is absent, which is a definitive negative inventory fact rather than an ambiguous binding.
issues.requirement_quote: If the signal transmission fails, it proceeds to the operational state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: One could argue NL2's three sentences ('it transitions...', 'if signal transmission fails...', 'once feedback is sent...') are all scoped to the Initial State's branching rather than a Braking State branch, since the closed model instead wires 'signal transmission fails' from InitialState; under that reading tr_0003 would satisfy an Initial-State-scoped guard obligation instead, but the contract as extracted binds this alternative to a Braking State source, and no such edge exists under that binding.
issues.title: No Braking State to Operational State edge exists in source or closed model

issues.basis: exact_source_inventory.transitions and inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions show no BrakingState->OperationalState edge; NL-CONTRACT-NL2-DERIVED-289ca4d960c6e21bfefb normative_statement requires this exact guarded transition.
issues.expected: The Braking State to Operational State transition must be guarded by the exact condition that signal transmission fails.
issues.observed: Because the complete transition inventory has no BrakingState->OperationalState edge at all (see companion endpoint candidate), there is no carrier transition on which any guard, present or absent, could be evaluated; the closed model instead attaches the Signal_Transmission_Fails trigger to InitialState->OperationalState (transition:line:14), which is a differently scoped transition and carries no separate guard field (guard=null).
issues.reason: S5 requires one exact existing transition ref to test its guard; since the required BrakingState->OperationalState edge does not exist, there is no transition ref to bind for S5, so this precise guard obligation must remain a predicate-null W1 candidate bound to the two endpoint states as the nearest exact carriers.
issues.requirement_quote: If the signal transmission fails, it proceeds to the operational state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: If the intended source were read as Initial State rather than Braking State, transition:line:14 would be the exact carrier and its guard field is null (event-only, no separate predicate), which would instead be a different, weaker guard-content gap on a different endpoint pair; under the contract's Braking-State-scoped binding as extracted, no carrier exists at all.
issues.title: No carrier transition exists to bear the required 'signal transmission fails' guard from Braking State to Operational State

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING (line 10, line 11); inspection_equivalent_facts.states outgoing_transition_refs=[] for ClampingState and ClampingLoseState; verify_facts.checks non_proved deadlock entries refuted with outgoing_count=0; canonical_source_ir.model.final_states=[]; NL1, NL3 quotes.
issues.expected: The basic braking device, framed as the final execution unit for ongoing train braking operations, should retain some operational continuation from every reachable operating state it enters, including the Brake Caliper Clamping State reached from the Braking State branch.
issues.observed: Deterministic facts show ClampingState (line 10) and ClampingLoseState (line 11) are both reachable from the initial state but have zero outgoing FCSTM transitions (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING diagnostics; verify_facts deadlock checks refuted with outgoing_count=0). Neither is declared a final/terminal state in the canonical source (final_states=[]), so both function as unmodeled permanent halts in an otherwise continuously operating control loop.
issues.reason: NL1 frames the whole model as a live, ongoing train braking control device, and NL3 requires the machine to progress into the Clamping state as part of that operating loop; the deterministic frontier facts show this reachable target (and the parallel ClampingLoseState leaf) has no way to continue or return to normal operation, which is a distinct behavioral-consequence defect from the already-satisfied endpoint-existence obligation.
issues.requirement_quote: After entering the braking state, the system transitions to the brake caliper clamping state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The NL text never explicitly states that the Brake Caliper Clamping State must resume behavior after clamping; the sentence 'After entering the braking state, the system transitions to the brake caliper clamping state' only describes reaching the state, so a competent reading treats ClampingState as an intentional narrative endpoint of this segment, and the underlying frozen predicate registry has no dedicated deadlock predicate for arbitrary leaf states absent an explicit progress/response clause, which is why this remains a predicate-null W1 candidate rather than a V1-backed claim.
issues.title: Reachable Brake Caliper Clamping State and Clamping Lose State are permanent dead ends with no outgoing continuation

contract_extraction.reason:
NL1 is descriptive context establishing the model's purpose (final execution unit for train braking), with no independently violable obligation. NL2 establishes an initial-entry to the braking state (from an implied root/initial pseudostate), a conditional endpoint to operational state on signal-transmission failure, and a return endpoint to the initial state upon signal feedback; the shared source for these branches is the braking state itself (entered via signal). NL3 establishes a sequential endpoint from braking state to brake caliper clamping state, continuing the discourse after entering braking state. Distinct transitions are represented as separate transition_endpoints contracts plus a transition_groups row capturing the shared-source alternatives from BrakingState (to OperationalState and back to InitialState is actually a different source - see below). I treat: (a) initial_entry contract for root/system -> initial state -> braking state pathway: actually the model's initial pseudostate enters the Initial State (explicit state), then upon receiving brake signal transitions to Braking State. NL2's "transitions from the initial state to the braking state" is an explicit transition endpoint (source=Initial State, target=Braking State), triggered by "receives a brake signal" (event). The "if signal transmission fails, proceeds to operational state" branches from Braking State (a different source, since it says "it" continuing from braking state context) -- but grammatically "it" refers to the basic braking device, and the alternative is presented right after the primary transition, suggesting it's an alternative outcome of the same signal-transmission attempt occurring while in Braking state. I model this as a separate endpoint contract source=Braking State, target=Operational State, guarded/triggered by signal transmission failure. The "once signal feedback is sent, it returns to initial state" is another endpoint from Braking State (or Operational State?) back to Initial State; given sequence, feedback happens after braking, so source=Braking State, target=Initial State. NL3 explicitly states after entering braking state, transitions to brake caliper clamping state, giving a further endpoint source=Braking State, target=Brake Caliper Clamping State. All these transitions share source Braking State except the very first (Initial State -> Braking State), so I form a transition_groups row for source=Braking State with alternatives: Operational State (on failure), Initial State (on feedback), Brake Caliper Clamping State (on entering, i.e. immediately). This preserves ordering and coreference without inventing evaluation content.</reason>

stage_receipts.reason:
NL1 is descriptive context establishing the model's purpose (final execution unit for train braking), with no independently violable obligation. NL2 establishes an initial-entry to the braking state (from an implied root/initial pseudostate), a conditional endpoint to operational state on signal-transmission failure, and a return endpoint to the initial state upon signal feedback; the shared source for these branches is the braking state itself (entered via signal). NL3 establishes a sequential endpoint from braking state to brake caliper clamping state, continuing the discourse after entering braking state. Distinct transitions are represented as separate transition_endpoints contracts plus a transition_groups row capturing the shared-source alternatives from BrakingState (to OperationalState and back to InitialState is actually a different source - see below). I treat: (a) initial_entry contract for root/system -> initial state -> braking state pathway: actually the model's initial pseudostate enters the Initial State (explicit state), then upon receiving brake signal transitions to Braking State. NL2's "transitions from the initial state to the braking state" is an explicit transition endpoint (source=Initial State, target=Braking State), triggered by "receives a brake signal" (event). The "if signal transmission fails, proceeds to operational state" branches from Braking State (a different source, since it says "it" continuing from braking state context) -- but grammatically "it" refers to the basic braking device, and the alternative is presented right after the primary transition, suggesting it's an alternative outcome of the same signal-transmission attempt occurring while in Braking state. I model this as a separate endpoint contract source=Braking State, target=Operational State, guarded/triggered by signal transmission failure. The "once signal feedback is sent, it returns to initial state" is another endpoint from Braking State (or Operational State?) back to Initial State; given sequence, feedback happens after braking, so source=Braking State, target=Initial State. NL3 explicitly states after entering braking state, transitions to brake caliper clamping state, giving a further endpoint source=Braking State, target=Brake Caliper Clamping State.
